title: Bruhat Interval Labels, Shellings, and Mobius Functions

items.title: Deleted-position labels from a fixed reduced expression, the lexicographic shelling criterion, and Mobius data

references.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
references.locator: Sections 2.2 and 2.5-2.7, printed pp. 33-36, 45 and 48-55 (augmentation and lifting; quotients; deleted-position labels of maximal chains; Lemma 2.7.2, Lemma 2.7.3, Lemma 2.7.4, Theorem 2.7.5, Corollaries 2.7.10-2.7.11 and Exercise 13), and Appendix A2.2-A2.4, printed pp. 302-305 (Mobius and shellability facts; cited, not consumed)

items.statement:
Let $W$ be the group presented by a Coxeter matrix $(S,m)$, with length function $\ell$, reflection set $T$ and Bruhat order $\le$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]], [[def-cg-bruhat-order-by-reflection-chains]]). Let $u\le v$ in $W$ and fix a reduced expression $v=s_1\cdots s_q$, where $q=\ell(v)$.

**(1) Maximal chains.** By [[lem-cg-bruhat-chain-refinement-and-gradedness]] the interval $[u,v]=\{x\in W:u\le x\le v\}$ ([[def-poset-interval-and-finiteness-conditions]]) is finite and graded with rank function $x\mapsto\ell(x)-\ell(u)$ ([[def-graded-poset-and-rank]]); a maximal chain of $[u,v]$ is a chain of covers $m\colon v=x_0\gtrdot x_1\gtrdot\cdots\gtrdot x_k=u$ with $k=\ell(v)-\ell(u)$, where $\gtrdot$ is the covering relation of [[def-graded-poset-and-rank]].

**(2) The deleted-position labeling.** Let $m\colon v=x_0\gtrdot x_1\gtrdot\cdots\gtrdot x_k=u$ be a maximal chain of $[u,v]$. Recursively, suppose that $P_j\subseteq\{1,\dots,q\}$ satisfies $|P_j|=q-j$ and that $x_j=\prod_{p\in P_j}s_p$ (product in increasing order of positions) is a reduced expression of $x_j$. By the cover criterion and reflection deletion of [[thm-cg-bruhat-lifting-and-cover-criterion]] (3), applied to the reduced expression $x_j=\prod_{p\in P_j}s_p$, the cover $x_j\gtrdot x_{j+1}$ determines a unique position $\lambda_{j+1}(m)\in P_j$ with $x_{j+1}=\prod_{p\in P_j\setminus\{\lambda_{j+1}(m)\}}s_p$, and this deletion word is a reduced expression of $x_{j+1}$; put $P_{j+1}:=P_j\setminus\{\lambda_{j+1}(m)\}$. This defines the **label word** $\lambda(m)=(\lambda_1(m),\dots,\lambda_k(m))$ of $m$. Its entries are pairwise distinct, because $P_0\supsetneq P_1\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq P_k$. Hence $m\mapsto\lambda(m)$ is a descending rooted-chain labeling of $[u,v]$ in the sense of [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (2), with values in the linearly ordered set $\{1,\dots,q\}$: a label is determined by the chain above its step and need not be a function of that step alone. The notions *increasing*, *falling*, *descent set* and the lexicographic order $\prec$ of label words are those of [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (3).

**(3) Rooted intervals.** If $u\le a<b\le v$ and $c$ is a descending chain from $v$ to $b$, the induced labeling of the rooted interval $([a,b],c)$ ([[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (2)) is again a deleted-position labeling of $[a,b]$: its labels are positions in the reduced expression of $b$ obtained from $v=s_1\cdots s_q$ by deleting the positions of the steps of $c$, and the label of a step of a maximal chain of $[a,b]$ is the position of the letter it deletes from that retained expression. Labels compared inside one rooted interval therefore belong to the one ordered set $\{1,\dots,q\}$. The labeling depends on the fixed reduced expression of $v$; no two label words obtained from different fixed expressions are compared anywhere on this page.

**(4) The lexicographic shelling criterion.** Let $K$ be a finite abstract simplicial complex ([[def-abstract-simplicial-complex]]) whose facets are listed in a linear order $F_1,\dots,F_t$. The order is a **shelling** of $K$, and $K$ is **shellable**, if for all $i<k$ there are $j<k$ and a vertex $x\in F_k$ with $F_i\cap F_k\subseteq F_j\cap F_k=F_k\setminus\{x\}$; this is the exact earlier-facet codimension-one intersection criterion. The facets of the order complex $\Delta([u,v])$ of $[u,v]$ are the maximal chains of $[u,v]$, and those of $\Delta((u,v))$ are the maximal chains of the open interval $(u,v)$ ([[def-face-poset-and-order-complex]]). The **lexicographic order of maximal chains** of $[u,v]$ is $m'\prec m:\iff\lambda(m')\prec\lambda(m)$.

**(5) Mobius data.** $\mu$ denotes the Mobius function of a finite poset ([[def-poset-mobius-function]]), so that on $[u,v]$ one has $\mu(x,x)=1$ and $\mu(x,y)=-\sum_{x\le z<y}\mu(x,z)$ for $x<y$ ([[lem-poset-mobius-recurrence]]).

This item asserts neither that the labeling satisfies the no-tie condition (N) or the lex-increasing property (L) of [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (4), nor that the lexicographic order is a shelling; both are proved in [[thm-cg-bruhat-deletion-label-shelling]], the recorded justifier of this definition, before any consumer uses them.
items.strategy:
A conventions-and-definitions item; the obligations are that the recursion of (2) is well defined and that the vocabulary of (1), (3)-(5) names already supplied objects. Everything is choice-free: the objects are predicates and subsets attached to the fixed group $W$, its fixed reduced expression and the finite interval $[u,v]$.

**(1)** Finiteness and grading are [[lem-cg-bruhat-chain-refinement-and-gradedness]] (1) and (3) verbatim; covers and maximal chains are as in [[def-graded-poset-and-rank]] and the interval notation as in [[def-poset-interval-and-finiteness-conditions]].

**(2)** Induction on $j$. For $j=0$ one has $P_0=\{1,\dots,q\}$ and $x_0=\prod_{p\in P_0}s_p$ is the fixed reduced expression of $v$. In the induction step the cover criterion and reflection deletion of [[thm-cg-bruhat-lifting-and-cover-criterion]] (3), applied to the reduced expression $x_j=\prod_{p\in P_j}s_p$ with $x_{j+1}$ in the role of an element covered by $x_j$, gives a unique $p_0\in P_j$ with $x_{j+1}=\prod_{p\in P_j\setminus\{p_0\}}s_p$ and with that deletion word reduced; this is exactly the induction step. The labels are pairwise distinct because the sets $P_j$ strictly decrease. Since $P_j$ is determined by $\lambda_1(m),\dots,\lambda_j(m)$, that is by the part of $m$ above $x_j$, the assignment is a descending rooted-chain labeling in the sense of [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (2); the possible dependence of the labeling on the chosen reduced expression of $v$ is stated explicitly, so no independence is asserted.

**(3)** Also by [[thm-cg-bruhat-lifting-and-cover-criterion]] (3), a descending chain $c$ from $v$ to $b$ deletes exactly the positions of its own steps, so the retained positions spell a reduced expression of $b$; the induced labeling of a rooted interval is therefore again by deleted positions, which is the rooted-interval convention of [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (2) instantiated in this labeling.

**(4)** The shelling vocabulary is the standard codimension-one facet-intersection criterion; the chain-shelling lemma [[lem-cg-lexicographic-chain-shelling-and-mobius-cancellation]] uses the same pairwise criterion for the order complex of a graded interval, and the facets named here are those of the order complex of [[def-face-poset-and-order-complex]]. No property of $K$, $\Delta([u,v])$ or $\Delta((u,v))$ is asserted by this clause.

**(5)** The published Mobius function and its recurrence ([[def-poset-mobius-function]], [[lem-poset-mobius-recurrence]]) are recalled for later use; they apply because all intervals in $W$ are finite by clause (1).

items.title: At most one increasing chain, rank-two diamonds, the lexicographically first chain, and the local descent replacement

references.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
references.locator: Sections 2.2 and 2.5-2.7, printed pp. 33-36, 45 and 48-55 (augmentation and lifting; quotients; deleted-position labels of maximal chains; Lemma 2.7.2, Lemma 2.7.3, Lemma 2.7.4, Theorem 2.7.5, Corollaries 2.7.10-2.7.11 and Exercise 13), and Appendix A2.2-A2.4, printed pp. 302-305 (Mobius and shellability facts; cited, not consumed)

items.statement:
Let $u<v$ in $W$, fix a reduced expression $v=s_1\cdots s_q$ and give $[u,v]$ the deleted-position labeling of [[def-cg-deletion-chain-labels-and-shelling]]. Let $([a,b],c)$ be a rooted interval of $[u,v]$ with its induced labeling (that item (3)): list its retained expression of the top $b$ in increasing order of the original positions as $t_1\cdots t_r$, so that $r=\ell(b)$ and the labels of the rooted interval are these original positions, an order-preserving relabelling that leaves every comparison of labels inside the one rooted interval unchanged; use *increasing*, *falling* and the lexicographic order of label words as in [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (3).

**(i) At most one increasing chain.** $([a,b],c)$ has at most one maximal chain whose label word is increasing.

**(ii) Rank-two intervals are diamonds.** If $\ell(b)-\ell(a)=2$, then $[a,b]$ has exactly four elements, and its two maximal chains have label words $(i,j)$ and $(p,m)$ with $i<j$, $m<p$ and $i<j\le p$; the first word is increasing and the second is falling.

**(iii) The lexicographically first chain.** $([a,b],c)$ has exactly one increasing maximal chain, and it is the lexicographically first maximal chain of $([a,b],c)$.

**(iv) Local descent replacement.** Let $m\colon b=m_0\gtrdot m_1\gtrdot\cdots\gtrdot m_k=a$ be a maximal chain of $([a,b],c)$ and let $1\le e<k$ with $\lambda_e(m)>\lambda_{e+1}(m)$; let $c_m$ be the root $c$ extended by the prefix $m_0\gtrdot\cdots\gtrdot m_{e-1}$, and write the unique increasing maximal chain of the rooted rank-two interval $([m_{e+1},m_{e-1}],c_m)$ as $m_{e-1}\gtrdot y\gtrdot m_{e+1}$. Then $k':=m_0\gtrdot\cdots\gtrdot m_{e-1}\gtrdot y\gtrdot m_{e+1}\gtrdot\cdots\gtrdot m_k$ is a maximal chain of $([a,b],c)$ with $\lambda(k')\prec\lambda(m)$ and $k'\cap m=m\setminus\{m_e\}$.
items.strategy: Follow the authored proof with retained positions relabelled in order. Cancellation 1.1 and induction 2.1 prove increasing uniqueness. Augmentation of a minimal last-deletion pair gives the increasing rank-two chain; word reversal and inversion give the unique falling chain (2.2,3.1). Step 4.1 proves the diamond and i<j<=p. Step 5.1 uses this rank-two base, then overlapping minimal prefix/suffix words only in ranks at least three. Step 6.1 extends the original root by the prefix and changes only the middle vertex; its first differing deleted-position label is smaller. Ranks zero/one and all deterministic finite choices are treated explicitly. All claims and suppliers are unchanged except the clarified root and element typing.
items.proof_strategy: deletion-position comparison, augmentation and mirrored construction, lexicographic minimality induction

items.title: Deletion-labeled Bruhat intervals are lexicographically shellable, with the explicit earlier/later chain comparison

references.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
references.locator: Sections 2.2 and 2.5-2.7, printed pp. 33-36, 45 and 48-55 (augmentation and lifting; quotients; deleted-position labels of maximal chains; Lemma 2.7.2, Lemma 2.7.3, Lemma 2.7.4, Theorem 2.7.5, Corollaries 2.7.10-2.7.11 and Exercise 13), and Appendix A2.2-A2.4, printed pp. 302-305 (Mobius and shellability facts; cited, not consumed)

items.statement:
Let $u\le v$ in $W$, put $n:=\ell(v)-\ell(u)$, fix a reduced expression of $v$ and give $[u,v]$ the deleted-position labeling of [[def-cg-deletion-chain-labels-and-shelling]], with label words, descents and the lexicographic order as in [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (3).

**(i) No-tie and lex-increasing conditions.** On every rooted interval of $[u,v]$ the labeling satisfies the no-tie condition (N) and the lex-increasing property (L) of [[def-cg-finite-lattice-congruence-and-interval-projections]] (4): the labels of any maximal chain are pairwise distinct, and there is exactly one increasing maximal chain, whose label word is lexicographically first.

**(ii) Earlier/later chain comparison.** For all maximal chains $m',m$ of $[u,v]$ with $\lambda(m')\prec\lambda(m)$ there is a maximal chain $k$ of $[u,v]$ with $\lambda(k)\prec\lambda(m)$, $m'\cap m\subseteq k\cap m$ and $|k\cap m|=|m|-1$.

**(iii) Shelling.** Consequently the maximal chains of the open interval $(u,v)$, in the lexicographic order of their label words, are a shelling of the order complex $\Delta((u,v))$ in the sense of [[def-cg-deletion-chain-labels-and-shelling]] (4), of which they are the facets; in particular $\Delta((u,v))$ is shellable.

**(iv) Small-rank conventions.** If $u=v$ or $n=1$, then $(u,v)$ is empty and $\Delta((u,v))=\{\varnothing\}$ has the single facet $\varnothing$, so its unique facet order is a shelling. If $n=2$, then $(u,v)$ has exactly two incomparable elements ([[lem-cg-bruhat-increasing-chain-and-local-descent-replacement]] (ii)) and $\Delta((u,v))$ consists of two disjoint vertices, shellable in either facet order.
items.strategy: For u<=v put n=ell(v)-ell(u). Steps 1.1-1.2 establish (N)/(L) on every root and injectivity of chain label words, with ranks zero and one explicit. Apply the proved abstract finite graded chain comparison lemma in step 2.1. Step 3.1 adjoins endpoints to identify open facets with closed maximal chains, then removes E={u,v} when n>=2: the unique omitted vertex is interior and both intersection and facet sizes drop by two. This proves the exact earlier-facet criterion. Rank zero/one give the single empty facet; rank two gives two disjoint vertices, shellable in either order. All fixed-word and root conventions are retained and no choice or unproved topology supplier is required.

items.title: Bruhat intervals are Eulerian: parity balance of the elements, and the Mobius function of a full interval

references.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
references.locator: Sections 2.2 and 2.5-2.7, printed pp. 33-36, 45 and 48-55 (augmentation and lifting; quotients; deleted-position labels of maximal chains; Lemma 2.7.2, Lemma 2.7.3, Lemma 2.7.4, Theorem 2.7.5, Corollaries 2.7.10-2.7.11 and Exercise 13), and Appendix A2.2-A2.4, printed pp. 302-305 (Mobius and shellability facts; cited, not consumed)

references.title: Yufei Zhao, On the Bruhat order of the symmetric group and its shellability (expository notes, MIT, 12 December 2007)
references.locator: Section 4, printed pp. 5-7 (Lemma 4.1 lifting property; Theorem 4.2, Verma's parity-balance induction in two cases; Corollary 4.3)

references.title: Brant C. Jones, An explicit derivation of the Mobius function for Bruhat order (arXiv:0904.4472v3, 11 December 2009)
references.locator: Sections 1-2, printed pp. 1-7 (Lemma 2.1 lifting lemma; Lemma 2.2 and Definitions 2.6-2.8 relative masks and the map phi; Theorem 2.12 complete matching; Corollary 2.13 sign formula)

items.statement:
Let $u\le v$ in $W$ and let $[u,v]=\{x\in W:u\le x\le v\}$ be the Bruhat interval ([[def-cg-bruhat-order-by-reflection-chains]], [[def-poset-interval-and-finiteness-conditions]]); it is finite by [[lem-cg-bruhat-chain-refinement-and-gradedness]] (1).

**(i) Cancellation formula.** $\sum_{x\in[u,v]}(-1)^{\ell(x)}=\delta_{u,v}(-1)^{\ell(u)}$; equivalently, if $u<v$ then $[u,v]$ contains equally many elements of even and of odd length ([[def-finite-cardinality]]), and $\sum_{x\in[u,v]}(-1)^{\ell(v)-\ell(x)}=\delta_{u,v}$.

**(ii) Mobius function of a full interval.** $\mu(u,v)=(-1)^{\ell(v)-\ell(u)}$, where $\mu$ is the Mobius function of the interval, computed from the recurrence of [[def-poset-mobius-function]] and [[lem-poset-mobius-recurrence]].

**(iii) Falling-chain form.** Equivalently, in the deleted-position labeling of [[def-cg-deletion-chain-labels-and-shelling]] the interval $[u,v]$ has exactly one strictly falling maximal chain: by the falling-chain formula of [[lem-cg-lexicographic-chain-shelling-and-mobius-cancellation]] (ii), instantiated through the shelling theorem [[thm-cg-bruhat-deletion-label-shelling]], one has $\mu(u,v)=(-1)^{\ell(v)-\ell(u)}\cdot\#\{\text{strictly falling maximal chains of }[u,v]\}$.

**(iv) Scope.** The sign formula is proved for the full Bruhat order on $W$, that is for intervals $[u,v]\subseteq W$. It is not asserted for intervals of a proper parabolic quotient $W^I$ ([[thm-cg-bruhat-parabolic-projection-and-quotients]]): there the fullness of the interval is an additional hypothesis, and the companion page exhibits a quotient interval for which the sign formula fails.
items.strategy: The authored lifting induction runs on ell(u)+ell(v). At a top right descent s, if us>u, z->zs pairs the full interval with opposite signs. If us<u, subtract the strip B=[us,v] minus [u,v], identify B inside [us,vs], and use smaller strictly ordered intervals after excluding diagonal coincidences. Diagonal intervals have their single sign term. Step 2.1 multiplies by (-1)^ell(v) for top normalization. The bottom-normalized signs satisfy the exact Mobius recurrence; uniqueness gives the sign formula. The proved finite graded (N)/(L) falling-chain formula, with root (v), then gives exactly one falling chain and the converse equivalence. No quotient fullness, topology theorem or choice principle is presumed.
items.proof_strategy: Verma's two-case lifting induction on the alternating sum, then the Mobius recurrence

items.title: All maximal chains of a rank-three interval in S4, their deleted-position labels, and the lexicographically first chain

references.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
references.locator: Sections 2.2 and 2.5-2.7, printed pp. 33-36, 45 and 48-55 (augmentation and lifting; quotients; deleted-position labels of maximal chains; Lemma 2.7.2, Lemma 2.7.3, Lemma 2.7.4, Theorem 2.7.5, Corollaries 2.7.10-2.7.11 and Exercise 13), and Appendix A2.2-A2.4, printed pp. 302-305 (Mobius and shellability facts; cited, not consumed)

items.statement:
Let $W=S_4$ with simple reflections $s_1=(1\,2)$, $s_2=(2\,3)$, $s_3=(3\,4)$ and one-line notation ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]), so that $\ell$ is the inversion number ([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (4), [[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). Put $c:=s_1s_2s_3=2341$, a reduced expression, and give the rank-three interval $[e,c]$ the deleted-position labeling induced by $c=s_1s_2s_3$ ([[def-cg-deletion-chain-labels-and-shelling]]).

**(i) The interval and its covers.** $[e,c]=\{1234;\ 2134,1324,1243;\ 2314,2143,1342;\ 2341\}$, where $2134=s_1$, $1324=s_2$, $1243=s_3$, $2314=s_1s_2$, $2143=s_1s_3$, $1342=s_2s_3$ and $2341=c$; the interval has eight elements and its covers are $2341\gtrdot1342$, $2341\gtrdot2143$, $2341\gtrdot2314$, $1342\gtrdot1243$, $1342\gtrdot1324$, $2143\gtrdot1243$, $2143\gtrdot2134$, $2314\gtrdot1324$, $2314\gtrdot2134$, and $s\gtrdot1234$ for each atom $s$. Hence $[e,c]$ has exactly six maximal chains.

**(ii) All label words.** The six maximal chains of $[e,c]$ with their label words are:
$$2341\gtrdot1342\gtrdot1243\gtrdot1234:\ (1,2,3),\qquad 2341\gtrdot1342\gtrdot1324\gtrdot1234:\ (1,3,2),$$
$$2341\gtrdot2143\gtrdot1243\gtrdot1234:\ (2,1,3),\qquad 2341\gtrdot2143\gtrdot2134\gtrdot1234:\ (2,3,1),$$
$$2341\gtrdot2314\gtrdot1324\gtrdot1234:\ (3,1,2),\qquad 2341\gtrdot2314\gtrdot2134\gtrdot1234:\ (3,2,1).$$
The six words are pairwise distinct and are exactly the six permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$; the unique falling one is $(3,2,1)$.

**(iii) Lexicographically first chain.** The lexicographically first maximal chain is $2341\gtrdot1342\gtrdot1243\gtrdot1234$ with label word $(1,2,3)$, and it is the unique increasing maximal chain ([[lem-cg-bruhat-increasing-chain-and-local-descent-replacement]] (i),(iii)).

**(iv) Local descent replacement.** The chain $2341\gtrdot1342\gtrdot1324\gtrdot1234$ has label word $(1,3,2)$, with a descent at position $2$. The rooted rank-two interval $[1234,1342]$ with retained expression $s_2s_3$ has the two middle elements $1324$ and $1243$, and its two maximal chains have label words $(3,2)$ (falling) and $(2,3)$ (increasing); replacing the falling segment $1342\gtrdot1324\gtrdot1234$ by the increasing chain $1342\gtrdot1243\gtrdot1234$ produces the lexicographically first chain, with word $(1,2,3)\prec(1,3,2)$, as in [[thm-cg-bruhat-deletion-label-shelling]] (ii) and [[lem-cg-bruhat-increasing-chain-and-local-descent-replacement]] (iv).
items.strategy:
All assertions are finite computations inside $[e,c]$ with the subword and cover criteria ([[thm-cg-bruhat-subword-characterization]], [[thm-cg-bruhat-lifting-and-cover-criterion]]); the finiteness and the grading by $\ell$ are [[lem-cg-bruhat-chain-refinement-and-gradedness]] (1),(3).

**(i)** Each of the eight displayed elements is the product of a subword of $s_1s_2s_3$, and each product is reduced of the displayed length, so all eight lie in $[e,c]$ by the subword characterization; conversely each element of $[e,c]$ is a product of a subword of the fixed reduced expression, and the eight subwords yield only these eight products (positions $\varnothing,\{1\},\{2\},\{3\},\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\},\{1,2,3\}$ evaluate to $1234,2134,1324,1243,2314,s_1s_3=2143,s_2s_3=1342,2341$). Covers: by the cover criterion (3) the elements covered by $c$ are exactly the single-letter deletions whose remaining word is reduced, namely $1342,2143,2314$ (deleting position $2$ leaves $s_1s_1s_3=s_3$ of length $1$, so it is not a cover); the remaining covers are checked the same way, and cover criterion (2) gives the converse, so the cover list is complete.

**(ii)** Each chain is evaluated as in (i), and each label is the position deleted at its step ([[def-cg-deletion-chain-labels-and-shelling]] (2)) relative to the retained word: $s_1s_2=2314$, $s_2s_3=1342$, $s_1s_3=2143$, $s_1=2134$, $s_2=1324$, $s_3=1243$, and the successive deletions give the six words listed, whose distinctness is read off the six permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$.

**(iii)** By (ii) the label words are the six permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$; the lexicographically first is $(1,2,3)$, and it is increasing, so (iii) is the statement of [[lem-cg-bruhat-increasing-chain-and-local-descent-replacement]] (iii) for this interval.

**(iv)** The retained expression of $1342$ is $s_2s_3$, with positions $2,3$ of the fixed word; its two maximal chains are $1342\gtrdot1324\gtrdot1234$, labelled $(3,2)$ (position $3$ deleted first, then position $2$), and $1342\gtrdot1243\gtrdot1234$, labelled $(2,3)$; here $2<3\le3$, as in [[lem-cg-bruhat-increasing-chain-and-local-descent-replacement]] (ii). Replacing the falling segment by the increasing chain keeps the first entry $1$ and changes the second entry from $3$ to $2$, so the new word $(1,2,3)$ is lexicographically smaller, which is the explicit instance of the replacement of [[thm-cg-bruhat-deletion-label-shelling]] (ii). No use of the Axiom of Choice is made.
items.proof_strategy: finite verification on the cover diagram of [e,2341] in S4

items.title: The Mobius value of the rank-three interval [e,c] in S4 from the recurrence, with the parity and falling-chain checks

references.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
references.locator: Sections 2.2 and 2.5-2.7, printed pp. 33-36, 45 and 48-55 (augmentation and lifting; quotients; deleted-position labels of maximal chains; Lemma 2.7.2, Lemma 2.7.3, Lemma 2.7.4, Theorem 2.7.5, Corollaries 2.7.10-2.7.11 and Exercise 13), and Appendix A2.2-A2.4, printed pp. 302-305 (Mobius and shellability facts; cited, not consumed)

references.title: Yufei Zhao, On the Bruhat order of the symmetric group and its shellability (expository notes, MIT, 12 December 2007)
references.locator: Section 4, printed pp. 5-7 (Lemma 4.1 lifting property; Theorem 4.2, Verma's parity-balance induction in two cases; Corollary 4.3)

items.statement:
In the notation of the type $A_3$ Coxeter group $W$ with simple reflections $s_1,s_2,s_3$ and one-line notation on the letters $\{1,2,3,4\}$ ([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (4), the published $S_4$ on $\{0,1,2,3\}$ under the letter shift $j\mapsto j-1$ of [[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]), let $c=s_1s_2s_3=2341$ and $[e,c]=\{1234;\ 2134,1324,1243;\ 2314,2143,1342;\ 2341\}$ ([[def-cg-deletion-chain-labels-and-shelling]]).

**(i) The recurrence.** With $\mu$ the Möbius function of $[e,c]$ ([[def-poset-mobius-function]], [[lem-poset-mobius-recurrence]]) one has $\mu(1234,1234)=1$; $\mu(1234,s)=-1$ for each atom $s\in\{s_1,s_2,s_3\}$; and $\mu(1234,x)=-(1-1-1)=1$ for each of the three rank-two elements $x$, because the elements of $[1234,x]$ are exactly $1234$, the two atoms covered by $x$ and $x$ itself. Hence $\mu(1234,2341)=-(1-3+3)=-1=(-1)^{\ell(2341)-\ell(1234)}=(-1)^3$, in agreement with [[thm-cg-bruhat-eulerian-intervals-and-mobius]] (ii).

**(ii) Parity balance.** $[e,c]$ has four elements of even length, $1234,2314,2143,1342$, and four of odd length, $2134,1324,1243,2341$; so the interval contains equally many elements of each parity, and $\sum_{x\in[e,c]}(-1)^{\ell(x)}=0$, as required by [[thm-cg-bruhat-eulerian-intervals-and-mobius]] (i) ([[def-finite-cardinality]]).

**(iii) Falling-chain check.** The unique strictly falling maximal chain of $[e,c]$ is $2341\gtrdot2314\gtrdot2134\gtrdot1234$ with label word $(3,2,1)$; the falling-chain formula of [[lem-cg-lexicographic-chain-shelling-and-mobius-cancellation]] (ii), applicable through [[thm-cg-bruhat-deletion-label-shelling]], gives $\mu(1234,2341)=(-1)^3\cdot1=-1$, consistent with (i) and with the count-one clause of [[thm-cg-bruhat-eulerian-intervals-and-mobius]] (iii).

items.title: A parabolic quotient interval of S4 whose Mobius value is 0, so the Eulerian sign formula does not extend to quotients

references.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
references.locator: Sections 2.2 and 2.5-2.7, printed pp. 33-36, 45 and 48-55 (augmentation and lifting; quotients; deleted-position labels of maximal chains; Lemma 2.7.2, Lemma 2.7.3, Lemma 2.7.4, Theorem 2.7.5, Corollaries 2.7.10-2.7.11 and Exercise 13), and Appendix A2.2-A2.4, printed pp. 302-305 (Mobius and shellability facts; cited, not consumed)

items.statement:
Let $W=S_4$ with $s_1=(1\,2)$, $s_2=(2\,3)$, $s_3=(3\,4)$ in one-line notation ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) and let $I=\{s_1,s_3\}$; write $W^I=\{w\in W:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in I\}$ for the parabolic quotient ([[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]], [[thm-cg-bruhat-parabolic-projection-and-quotients]] (1),(4)).

**(i) The quotient interval.** $W^I=\{1234,1324,1423,2314,2413,3412\}$, of lengths $0,1,2,2,3,4$ ([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (4), [[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]), and $3412$ is its greatest element, so the quotient interval $[1234,3412]^I=W^I$ has six elements with covers $1234\lessdot1324$, $1324\lessdot1423$, $1324\lessdot2314$, $1423\lessdot2413$, $2314\lessdot2413$ and $2413\lessdot3412$.

**(ii) The Mobius values.** Computing the Mobius function of the induced poset ([[def-poset-mobius-function]], [[lem-poset-mobius-recurrence]]) gives $\mu(1234,1234)=1$, $\mu(1234,1324)=-1$ and $\mu(1234,1423)=\mu(1234,2314)=\mu(1234,2413)=\mu(1234,3412)=0$. In particular $\mu(1234,3412)=0$, whereas $(-1)^{\ell(3412)-\ell(1234)}=(-1)^4=1$.

**(iii) The refuted claim and the dropped hypothesis.** Hence the conclusion of [[thm-cg-bruhat-eulerian-intervals-and-mobius]] (ii) does not extend from full Bruhat intervals to intervals in a proper parabolic quotient; the indiscriminate form '$\mu(x,y)=(-1)^{\ell(y)-\ell(x)}$ for every interval of every quotient' is false, and the precise dropped hypothesis is fullness: $[1234,3412]^I$ is a proper subset of the full interval $[1234,3412]$, since $1432=s_2s_3s_2$ satisfies $1432\le3412$ (it is the product of the subword at positions $1,3,4$ of the reduced expression $3412=s_2s_1s_3s_2$, [[thm-cg-bruhat-subword-characterization]]) but $1432\notin W^I$, because $\ell(1432\,s_3)=\ell(1423)=2<3=\ell(1432)$. For full intervals the formula holds by the cited theorem.
items.strategy:
All assertions are finite computations in the six-element quotient interval; the quotient order is the restriction of the Bruhat order and is graded of rank four ([[thm-cg-bruhat-parabolic-projection-and-quotients]] (1),(3)).

**(i)** $w\in W^I$ means $\ell(ws_1)>\ell(w)$ and $\ell(ws_3)>\ell(w)$, that is, no right descent at $s_1$ or $s_3$; equivalently $w(1)<w(2)$ and $w(3)<w(4)$ in one-line notation, and testing the $24$ permutations of $S_4$ leaves exactly the six displayed elements, with the displayed lengths ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). Each displayed cover is a Bruhat cover in $W$ by the cover criterion (a single letter is deleted and the remaining word is reduced), and there are no further covers inside $W^I$: an element covered by another in $W^I$ has lengths differing by one and lies between the two, and the only such elements are those displayed, since $W^I$ has six elements in ranks $0,1,2,2,3,4$ by [[thm-cg-bruhat-parabolic-projection-and-quotients]] (3).

**(ii)** The recurrence computes the values in increasing length: $\mu(1234,1324)=-1$; $\mu(1234,1423)=-(\mu(1234,1234)+\mu(1234,1324))=-(1-1)=0$ and likewise $\mu(1234,2314)=0$; $\mu(1234,2413)=-(1-1+0+0)=0$; finally $\mu(1234,3412)=-(1-1+0+0+0)=0$. The exponent $\ell(3412)-\ell(1234)=4$ uses the inversion number ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]).

**(iii)** $1432\le3412$ by the subword characterization [[thm-cg-bruhat-subword-characterization]], using the reduced expression $3412=s_2s_1s_3s_2$ and its subword $s_2s_3s_2=1432$ at positions $1,3,4$; and $\ell(1432\,s_3)=\ell(1423)=2<3=\ell(1432)$ shows $1432\notin W^I$, so the quotient interval is properly contained in the full interval. This is the exact failure of the indiscriminate Eulerian claim and the reason the theorem [[thm-cg-bruhat-eulerian-intervals-and-mobius]] restricts its scope in clause (iv). No use of the Axiom of Choice is made.
